headline: Indonesia halts BDx's 640MW AI data center over missing permits
body: West Java's governor ordered Singapore's BDx Data Centers to stop construction on a 640 megawatt AI data center campus in Jatiluhur after it broke ground on September 22 without the required permits. Governor Dedi Mulyadi said the work must stop until permits and an environmental impact assessment are completed, not because of any environmental violation.
note: Indonesia wants the AI data center investment but is still building the permitting process to go with it, and similar friction over power and water has already slowed projects in Malaysia. For banks financing the region's AI buildout, approvals are becoming as big a timeline risk as construction.

evidence.text: A governor of Indonesia's most populous province has ordered Singapore's BDx Data Centers to halt construction on a data ‌centre due to a lack of required permits, amid a push ‌by Southeast Asia's largest economy to catch up with regional peers in technology infrastructure projects.

BDx, ​which runs data centres for cloud companies and other large businesses across Asia, said it broke ground on a 640-megawatt artificial intelligence (AI) data-centre campus in Jatiluhur in West Java on September 22.

In a video of a meeting posted to Instagram on Wednesday, ‌Governor Dedi Mulyadi of West ⁠Java told BDx representatives that construction work had to stop until required permits were obtained and the project's environmental impact assessment ⁠process was completed.

"The project is being halted not because it violates ​environmental ​rules. It's being halted because the permits ​have not yet been issued," Dedi ‌said in a separate video that was posted on YouTube on Tuesday.
Opposition to data centres has emerged elsewhere in Southeast Asia, including in Malaysia, the region's fastest-growing data-centre market.
